Gürcü yedek birlikleri Tiflis çevresinde mevzilendi.

moments.title: Terörle Mücadele Rejiminin Sonu
moments.text: 16 Nisan 2009: Medvedev Çeçenistan'daki 'terörle mücadele operasyonu' rejimini resmen sona erdirdi. Ramzan Kadirov bölgenin tam kontrolünde; Grozni yeniden inşa edildi; ama Dağıstan, İnguşetya ve Kabardin-Balkar'da şiddet sürüyor.

Russia.text: On yıllık savaş resmen bitti; bedeli çok büyük, ama Çeçenistan Rusya içinde kaldı. Sorun şimdi Ramzan Kadirov'un Moskova'ya olan bağımlılığı ve diğer cumhuriyetlerde yayılan şiddet.

options.r: Kremlin Çeçenistan'da 'normalleşme'yi ilan etti.

options.t: Kuzey Kafkasya'ya kalkınma ve güvenlik paketi
options.r: Moskova Kuzey Kafkasya için yeni bir federal kalkınma programı açıkladı.

custom_0.text: Direniş bölünmüş ve zayıf; bağımsızlık fikri Ramzan'ın baskısı altında. Yine de Umarov'un Emirliği Kafkasya'da hâlâ ayakta.

options.r: Dağlarda küçük çeteler Rus ve Kadirovtsi hedeflerine saldırmayı sürdürüyor.
Çeçen komutanların bir kısmı Kadirov'un afından yararlandı.

en.Rus uçakları ve Dağıstan milisleri Botli: Russian aircraft and Dagestani militias pushed Basayev back at Botlikh.
en.Çeçen hükümetinden Basayev'i durdurmasın: Ask Grozny to rein in Basayev
en.Moskova Maskhadov'dan Basayev'i kontrol: Moscow asked Maskhadov to control Basayev.
en.Dağıstan'ın dağlarında köyler elden gidi: Villages are slipping away in the mountains of Dagestan. Yeltsin is weak and Putin is barely known. The army wants revenge for 1996.
en.Baskını kınama, Maskhadov'la git (tarihî: Condemn the raid and distance Grozny (historical)
en.Maskhadov Dağıstan baskınını 'Grozni'nin: Maskhadov said the Dagestan raid was 'not Grozny's business'.
en.Çeçen gönüllüler Dağıstan'ın Botlih ve N: Chechen volunteers flow towards Dagestan's Botlikh and Novolak districts.
en.Maskhadov Basayev'in baskınını kınadı am: Maskhadov condemned Basayev's raid but cannot control him. Radicals in the Shura talk of 'liberating Dagestan'; Maskhadov's authority is weak.
en.7 Ağustos 1999: Şamil Basayev ve Arap ko: 7 August 1999: about 1,500 fighters under Shamil Basayev and the Arab commander Khattab entered the mountainous Botlikh area of Dagestan and proclaimed an 'Islamic state'. On 9 August Yeltsin dismissed Prime Minister Stepashin and appointed Vladimir Putin.
en.Çeçenistan'a hava ve kara harekâtı: Air and ground operation into Chechnya
en.Rus uçakları Çeçenistan'ı bombalıyor; 30: Russian aircraft are bombing Chechnya; on 30 September armoured columns crossed the Terek.
en.Önce Rusya'da güvenlik, ortak soruşturma: Security at home and a joint inquiry first
en.Moskova Maskhadov'la ortak soruşturma ön: Moscow offered Maskhadov a joint inquiry; the public is impatient.
en.Ülke şokta, kamuoyu intikam istiyor. 'Te: The country is in shock and public opinion demands revenge. The decision on a 'counter-terrorist operation' will define Putin.
en.Maskhadov seferberlik ilan etti; 'gazava: Maskhadov declared mobilisation; a call for 'ghazavat' was made.
en.Ortak soruşturma ve barış çağrısı: Call for a joint inquiry and peace
en.Maskhadov Putin'e görüşme önerdi; Moskov: Maskhadov proposed a meeting to Putin; Moscow did not reply.
en.Patlamalarla ilgisiniz yok ama Rus basın: You had nothing to do with the bombings but the Russian press blames the Chechens. Maskhadov offered a joint inquiry to Moscow; a major attack is clearly being prepared.
en.Ankara 'terörle mücadele'yi Rusya'nın ha: Ankara described counter-terrorism as Russia's right.
en.Türkiye Çeçen mültecilere insani yardım: Turkey sent humanitarian aid to Chechen refugees.
en.17 Ağustos depremi (17 bin ölü) Türkiye': The 17 August earthquake (17,000 dead) wounded Turkey, which is struggling to recover. Developments in Chechnya revive reaction in the diaspora.
en.4–16 Eylül 1999: Buynaksk, Moskova (iki: 4–16 September 1999: bombings of apartment blocks in Buynaksk, Moscow (twice) and Volgodonsk killed about 300 people. Putin vowed to 'hunt them down even in the outhouse'; responsibility is still disputed, but the public wants war.
en.Kuzeyi güvenceye al, Grozni'yi kuşat (ta: Secure the north and encircle Grozny (historical)
en.Rus birlikleri Terek'in kuzeyini ele geç: Russian troops took the north bank of the Terek and began encircling Grozny.
en.Moskova İnguşetya sınırında güvenli geçi: Moscow declared a safe passage on the Ingush border.
en.Birinci savaştan farklı: hava ve topçu ö: Unlike the first war: air and artillery first, infantry afterwards. The press cannot roam freely and casualty news is limited. Putin's ratings are rising.
en.Dağlarda direnişe geç, şehri boşalt: Shift to the mountains, evacuate Grozny
en.Maskhadov güçlerini güneye ve dağlara ka: Maskhadov is shifting his forces to the south and the mountains.
en.Ordunun kuzeyi kayıpsız aldı; Maskhadov: The army took the north without loss; Maskhadov is building a new defence line in the southern mountains. Refugees stream south or into Ingushetia.
en.Mültecileri kabul et, sınırı kontrol et: Take in refugees, control the border
en.Gürcistan mültecilere sınır kapısını açt: Georgia opened its border to refugees.
en.Çeçen mültecilerin bir kısmı Pankisi Vad: Some Chechen refugees are crossing into the Pankisi Gorge; Russia accuses Georgia of giving fighters a 'safe haven'.
en.30 Eylül'de Rus zırhlı sütunları Çeçenis: On 30 September Russian armoured columns occupied northern Chechnya (Nadterechny, Naursky, Shelkovskaya). On 21 October the Central Market in Grozny was hit by missiles, killing hundreds of civilians. More than 200,000 refugees poured into Ingushetia.
en.Zirveyi başarıyla topla, nazik uyarı (ta: Run the summit smoothly with a mild warning (historical)
en.Zirvede BTC boru hattı anlaşması imzalan: The BTC pipeline deal was signed at the summit; Turkey became a key Caucasus player.
en.Çeçenistan'ı gündemin merkezine koy: Put Chechnya at the centre of the agenda
en.Ankara zirvede Çeçenistan'daki sivil kay: Ankara used strong language over civilian casualties in Chechnya.
en.Ankara zirveyi enerji ve ticaret gündemi: Ankara focused the summit on energy and trade.
en.Ev sahibisiniz: Clinton, Yeltsin, Şröder: You are the host: Clinton, Yeltsin, Schröder, Chirac and the Caucasian leaders are in Istanbul. The pipeline serves Turkey's energy-corridor goal while Chechnya casts a shadow over the stage.
en.AKKA'yı imzala, Çeçenistan'ı 'iç mesele': Sign CFE; call Chechnya an internal matter (historical)
en.Zirvede savaşı savun: Defend the war at the summit
en.Yeltsin zirvede 'Rusya terörle mücadele: Yeltsin dismissed the criticism, saying 'Russia is fighting terrorism'.
en.Gürcistan üslerini kapat, Batı'yı yumuşa: Pledge to close Georgian bases to soften the West
en.Rusya Gürcistan'daki iki üssünü kapatma: Russia promised to close two bases in Georgia.
en.Yeltsin'in son büyük sahnesi: Batı'nın e: Yeltsin's last big scene: he will call the criticism interference and defend Putin's war. A commitment on the Georgian bases would soften the West.
en.Clinton zirvede Çeçenistan'da siyasî çöz: Clinton called for a political solution in Chechnya; Yeltsin was furious.
en.Washington zirvede silah kontrol anlaşma: Washington focused on the arms-control deal at the summit.
en.Clinton, Yeltsin'in 'Çeçenistan'da sivil: Clinton considers publicly criticising Yeltsin's hard line against civilians in Chechnya, yet Russia's nuclear arsenal and reforms remain priorities.
en.18–19 Kasım 1999: AGİT İstanbul Zirvesi': 18–19 November 1999: at the OSCE Istanbul Summit Clinton and Yeltsin clashed over Chechnya; the Adapted CFE Treaty was signed, and an intergovernmental agreement for the Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline was signed. Russia pledged to close its bases in Georgia.
en.Rus topçusu Grozni'yi haftalarca dövdü;: Russian artillery pounded Grozny for weeks; the city turned to rubble.
en.Moskova sivillerin çıkışı için güvenli k: Moscow offered a safe corridor for civilians.
en.Putin yılbaşı gecesi iktidarı devraldı;: Putin took power on New Year's Eve; the army has Grozny encircled. To avoid repeating the first war's mistake, the plan is to crush the city with artillery rather than enter block by block.
en.Basayev ve Gelayev şehirde direnişi örgü: Basayev and Gelayev organised the resistance inside the city.
en.Şehri boşalt, güneyde direniş kur: Break out and resist in the south
en.Maskhadov güçlerini şehirden çıkarmayı p: Maskhadov plans to withdraw his forces from the city.
en.Grozni bir ölüm tuzağına dönüşebilir: ku: Grozny may turn into a death trap: besieged, with both armed forces and hundreds of thousands of civilians. Maskhadov looks for exits to save his forces.
en.6 Aralık: Rusya Grozni sakinlerine şehri: 6 December: Russia gave Grozny's residents an ultimatum to leave by 11 December; artillery and air strikes followed. On 31 December Boris Yeltsin resigned and Putin became acting president.
en.Rus birlikleri güney dağlarına ilerliyor: Russian forces advance into the southern mountains.
en.Siyasî çözüm: yerel yönetim kur: A political solution: set up local authority
en.Kremlin Çeçen eşrafıyla yeni bir yönetim: The Kremlin approached Chechen elders to set up a new administration.
en.Grozni sizin, ama şehrin yarısı enkaz. D: Grozny is yours but half the city is rubble. The resistance will go on in the mountains and villages; mines and ambushes will cost casualties.
en.Çeçen müfrezeleri dağlara çekilip köyler: Chechen detachments withdrew into the mountains and dispersed into villages.
en.Maskhadov Putin'e koşulsuz ateşkes önerd: Maskhadov offered Putin an unconditional ceasefire; the Kremlin refused.
en.Şehir kaybedildi; ordunun parçalanması,: The city is lost; the army's fragmentation increases the sway of warlords and radicals. Maskhadov tries to keep unity in the mountains.
en.Ocak sonunda Çeçen kuvvetleri Grozni'den: At the end of January Chechen forces broke out of Grozny towards Alkhan-Kala but suffered heavy losses in a minefield (Basayev lost a foot). On 6 February Russia declared Grozny captured.
en.Putin yedi federal bölge kurarak valiler: Putin set up seven federal districts to rein in the governors.
en.Kremlin Çeçenistan'da yeni bir yönetici: The Kremlin is looking for a new administrator in Chechnya.
en.Zaferle seçildiniz; Çeçenistan dosyası a: You won decisively; the Chechnya file is now framed as 'fighting terrorism'. It is time to tame oligarchs and governors.
en.26 Mart 2000: Putin ilk turda %53 oyla c: 26 March 2000: Putin was elected president in the first round with 53%. In early March Chechen units were encircled and destroyed at Komsomolskoye; on 1 March Pskov paratroopers took heavy losses at Ulus-Kert.
en.Kadirov'un milisleri Rus birlikleriyle b: Kadyrov's militias began operating alongside Russian forces.
en.Yeterince asker, yerel aracı yok: Plenty of troops, no local broker
en.Genelkurmay yerel aracıları reddetti; op: The General Staff rejected local brokers; operations go on.
en.Çeçen yanlısı yönetim size iç kamuoyunda: A pro-Moscow Chechen administration gives you 'normalisation' at home, yet Kadyrov's autonomy may cause trouble later.
en.Kadirov'u 'hain' ilan et, suikast örgütl: Brand Kadyrov a traitor and organise assassinations
en.Maskhadov ve Basayev Kadirov'a karşı ölü: Maskhadov and Basayev issued a death sentence against Kadyrov.
en.Halkı sahiplen, eşrafla uzlaş: Win over the elders and clans
en.Maskhadov eşraf ve köy büyüklerini bir a: Maskhadov convened gatherings of elders and village leaders.
en.Çeçen toplumunda bölünme: eski müftü Mos: Division in Chechen society: the former mufti has switched to Moscow and some local clans are joining Kadyrov. The resistance faces a rival from within.
en.12 Haziran 2000: Putin eski Çeçen müftüs: 12 June 2000: Putin appointed Akhmad Kadyrov, the former Chechen mufti, as Chechnya's 'head of administration'. He had opposed Maskhadov's call for jihad and switched to Moscow; the policy of 'Chechenisation' began.
en.Terörle savaşta işbirliği: Cooperate in the war on terror
en.Putin Bush'a istihbarat ve hava sahası d: Putin offered Bush intelligence and airspace support.
en.Batı'ya güvenme: Do not rely on the West
en.Moskova ABD'nin Orta Asya'ya yerleşmesin: Moscow objected to America settling in Central Asia.
en.Batı'nın dikkati Afganistan'a kaydı; Çeç: The West's attention has turned to Afghanistan; Chechnya is now part of 'Russia's fight against international terrorism'. What can you get from the West in exchange for accepting US bases in Central Asia?
en.Maskhadov 11 Eylül'ü kınayıp 'Çeçenistan: Maskhadov condemned 9/11 and said Chechnya is not a terrorist organisation.
en.Radikal komutanlar cihat söylemini sertl: Radical commanders hardened their jihadist rhetoric.
en.Dünya sizi artık 'el-Kaide bağlantılı' g: The world now sees you as 'al-Qaeda linked'; the presence of Khattab and Arab volunteers reinforces that view. Western sympathy is melting fast.
en.ABD 'Train and Equip' programını kabul e: Accept the US 'Train and Equip' programme (historical)
en.ABD Özel Kuvvetleri Gürcü askerlerini eğ: US Special Forces began training Georgian soldiers.
en.Tiflis Moskova'yla Pankisi'de ortak güve: Tbilisi proposed a joint security operation in Pankisi.
en.Pankisi Vadisi'nde Çeçen mülteciler ve s: There are Chechen refugees and armed groups in the Pankisi Gorge; Russia pushes the 'terrorist haven' line. Shevardnadze sees a chance to move closer to the US.
en.Bush Putin'i Teksas'taki çiftliğine dave: Bush invited Putin to his Texas ranch.
en.Kongre'de Rusya yardımına Çeçenistan şar: A Chechnya condition on Russia aid was proposed in Congress.
en.Bush ve Putin ortaklık kuruyor; Rusya Af: Bush and Putin are building a partnership; Russia is key in Afghanistan. Human rights abuses in Chechnya are questioned in Congress and the press.
en.11 Eylül 2001'den sonra Putin Bush'u ara: After 9/11 Putin was the first leader to call Bush; Western criticism of Chechnya softened. In 2001–02 Russia reacted to Chechen and Arab fighters in Georgia's Pankisi Gorge; the US launched a 'Train and Equip' programme in Georgia.
en.Rus özel kuvvetleri gaz verip tiyatroya: Russian special forces pumped in gas and stormed the theatre; most hostages survived but hundreds were hospitalised.
en.Moskova arabuluculara izin verdi; ama kr: Moscow allowed intermediaries, but time is running out.
en.Moskova'nın kalbinde rehine krizi; kamuo: A hostage crisis in the heart of Moscow; the public is both helpless and furious. A raid is risky; negotiation means 'concession'.
en.Saldırıyı kınama, rehineleri koruma çağr: Condemn the raid and urge protection of hostages
en.Maskhadov rehinelerin serbest bırakılmas: Maskhadov called for the hostages' release.
en.Basayev eylemi 'Rusya'ya bir mesaj' olar: Basayev presented the action as 'a message to Russia'.
en.Maskhadov rehine almayı onaylamadığını a: Maskhadov said he did not approve of hostage-taking, yet Basayev claimed the attack. It may badly damage the international image of the Chechen cause.
en.23–26 Ekim 2002: Movsar Barayev komutası: 23–26 October 2002: about 40 Chechens under Movsar Barayev seized the Dubrovka theatre in Moscow, taking 850 hostages. On the third day Russian special forces stormed it after pumping in an incapacitating gas; about 130 hostages died.
en.Kremlin referandumu 'normalleşmenin kanı: The Kremlin presented the referendum as 'proof of normalisation'.
en.Moskova Grozni'nin yeniden inşası için y: Moscow announced new funds for rebuilding Grozny.
en.Referandum Çeçenistan'ı 'hukuken' Rusya': The referendum legally ties Chechnya to Russia; though the West criticises the contested vote, Putin's position is strengthened.
en.Maskhadov referandumu 'işgal altında yap: Maskhadov called the referendum 'theatre under occupation'.
en.Çeçen müfrezeleri Rus konvoylarına pusu: Chechen detachments keep ambushing Russian convoys.
en.Referandum Rus ordusunun gölgesinde yapı: The referendum was held in the army's shadow; the resistance's political wing is marginalised. Maskhadov tries to address the people from hiding.
en.23 Mart 2003: Çeçenistan'ın Rusya'nın bi: 23 March 2003: a referendum on a constitution declaring Chechnya a part of Russia passed with 96% 'yes'; the vote, held under heavy military presence in a war-weary population, is disputed. On 5 October Akhmad Kadyrov was elected 'president' with 80%.
en.Kremlin Alu Alhanov'u 'Çeçen cumhurbaşka: The Kremlin backed Alu Alkhanov as 'Chechen president'.
en.Ramzan'ın 'Kadirovtsi' milisleri güvenli: Ramzan's 'Kadyrovtsy' militias took the lead in security.
en.Çeçenleştirme politikasının mimarı öldü;: The architect of Chechenisation is dead; Ramzan Kadyrov is ready to fill the vacuum. The insurgency is spreading to Ingushetia.
en.İnguşetya'da yeni cephe aç (tarihî): Open a new front in Ingushetia (historical)
en.Basayev'in adamları Nazran'da polis ve g: Basayev's men stormed police and security posts in Nazran.
en.Maskhadov'un adamları güney dağlarında m: Maskhadov's men held their positions in the southern mountains.
en.Suikast direnişin başarısı, ama Rusya'nı: The assassination is a success for the resistance, but Russian retaliation will harden. Basayev aims to open new fronts: Ingushetia and Kabardino-Balkaria.
en.9 Mayıs 2004: Grozni'de Zafer Günü tören: 9 May 2004: a bomb at the Victory Day ceremony in Grozny's stadium killed Akhmad Kadyrov. In June Basayev's units raided Nazran, Ingushetia (21–22 June); in August Alu Alkhanov was elected president of Chechnya.
en.Putin valilerin doğrudan seçimini kaldır: Putin abolished direct election of governors and hardened counter-terror laws.
en.Kremlin'in bir kanadı Maskhadov'la gizli: One Kremlin faction proposed secret contact with Maskhadov; Putin refused.
en.Savaşın en korkunç anı: kamuoyu sarsıldı: The war's most terrible moment: public shock and Western sympathy. Putin's response: centralisation.
en.Saldırıyı kınama, Basayev'den ayrıl: Condemn it and distance from Basayev
en.Maskhadov Beslan'ı kınayıp 'sivil hedefl: Maskhadov condemned Beslan, saying he opposes attacks on civilians.
en.Radikal komutanlar saldırıyı 'savaşın do: Radical commanders called the attack 'a natural result of the war'.
en.Basayev sorumluluk üstlendi; Maskhadov s: Basayev claimed responsibility; Maskhadov condemned the attack, but that can no longer save the resistance's image. Support for the Chechen cause in the West and the Muslim world is falling fast.
en.1–3 Eylül 2004: Kuzey Osetya'nın Beslan: 1–3 September 2004: a group acting in Basayev's name seized School No. 1 in Beslan, North Ossetia, taking 1,100 hostages. On the third day explosions and gunfire killed 334 people, nearly half of them children.
en.Tutumu sürdür, af ve milisler (tarihî): Press on with amnesty and militias (historical)
en.Moskova yeni af ilan etti; Kadirovtsi'le: Moscow declared a new amnesty; the Kadyrovtsy run operations.
en.Rus iç birlikleri dağlarda yeni operasyo: Russian interior troops began new mountain operations.
en.Putin 'direnişin başı' diye kutladı; Mas: Putin hailed 'the head of the resistance'; the door to talks with Maskhadov is shut for good. The insurgency is drifting toward Basayev and the Islamists.
en.Basayev bütün askerî harekâtı yönetmeye: Basayev began directing all military operations.
en.Maskhadov'un ölümü direnişin ılımlı kana: Maskhadov's death destroyed the moderate wing. Sadulayev is a young cleric but Basayev commands in the field.
en.8 Mart 2005: Çeçen direnişinin seçilmiş: 8 March 2005: Aslan Maskhadov, the resistance's elected leader, was killed by Russian special forces in a bunker in Tolstoy-Yurt. Abdul-Halim Sadulayev succeeded him.
en.Moskova Çeçenistan'da askerî varlığı aza: Moscow reduced its military presence and left security to Ramzan Kadyrov.
en.Rus servisleri Kuzey Kafkasya'da yeni op: Russian services began new operations across the North Caucasus.
en.Savaşın iki kilit ismi ortadan kalktı. K: Two key figures of the war are gone. The Kremlin will say 'the war is over'; but young militants and a network across the Caucasus are rebuilding.
en.Umarov'u destekle, Kafkas cephesi kur: Back Umarov and build a Caucasus front
en.Umarov Dağıstan, İnguşetya ve Kabardin-B: Umarov began joining cells in Dagestan, Ingushetia and Kabardino-Balkaria.
en.Bazı komutanlar Moskova'nın af teklifler: Some commanders opened the door to Moscow's amnesty offers.
en.Direniş lidersiz kaldı. Doku Umarov, Kaf: The resistance is leaderless. Doku Umarov tries to build an Islamic front across the whole Caucasus; Chechen nationalism recedes.
en.Saydullayev ve Basayev'in Sonu: The End of Sadulayev and Basayev
en.17 Haziran 2006: Saydullayev Argun'da öl: 17 June 2006: Sadulayev was killed in Argun; Doku Umarov succeeded him. On 10 July Basayev died in an explosion in the Ingush village of Ekazhevo; Russian officials claimed the operation. Two charismatic leaders disappeared within weeks.
en.Çeçen modelini komşulara uygula: Apply the Chechen model next door
en.Moskova Ramzan Kadirov'a Çeçenistan'da g: Moscow gave Ramzan Kadyrov wide powers in Chechnya.
en.Kremlin Kuzey Kafkasya için yeni bir kal: The Kremlin announced a new development fund for the North Caucasus.
en.Çeçenistan Ramzan'ın kontrolünde 'sakin': Chechnya is 'calm' under Ramzan, but the violence is moving to Dagestan and Ingushetia. This is a new, more diffuse version of the war the Kremlin claims is solved.
en.Umarov'un çağrısıyla Dağıstan ve İnguşet: New cells were set up in Dagestan and Ingushetia at Umarov's call.
en.Sürgündeki Çeçen hükümeti Umarov'un 'emi: The Chechen government in exile objected to Umarov's 'emirate'.
en.Umarov bir 'emirlik' ilan etti: Çeçen ba: Umarov proclaimed an 'emirate': the Chechen independence idea has morphed into something else. Yet Chechen society is war-weary and under Kadyrov's pressure.
en.15 Şubat 2007: Ramzan Kadirov Çeçenistan: 15 February 2007: Ramzan Kadyrov became president of Chechnya. On 31 October Doku Umarov proclaimed the 'Caucasus Emirate': the Chechen independence cause was dropped in favour of an Islamic jihad covering the whole North Caucasus.
en.Gürcü birlikleri Tskhinvali'ye taarruz e: Georgian troops attacked Tskhinvali; Russian armour entered through the Roki tunnel.
en.Tiflis son anda Tskhinvali taarruzunu ip: Tbilisi called off the Tskhinvali offensive at the last moment.
en.Saakaşvili Güney Osetya'da 'anayasal düz: Saakashvili wants to restore 'constitutional order' in South Ossetia; the West has given encouragement but the Russian army can come through the Roki tunnel.
en.Rus birlikleri Gori'ye kadar ilerledi; B: Russian forces advanced to Gori; the West spoke harshly.
en.Moskova yalnızca Güney Osetya'daki barış: Moscow only reinforced its peacekeepers in South Ossetia.
en.Medvedev cumhurbaşkanı, Putin başbakan;: Medvedev is president, Putin prime minister; Georgia's NATO path (the April 2008 Bucharest summit) bothers the Kremlin. If fighting breaks out in South Ossetia, the response is ready.
en.Erdoğan Kafkasya İstikrar ve İşbirliği P: Erdoğan proposed the Caucasus Stability and Cooperation Platform.
en.Ankara Gürcistan'ın toprak bütünlüğünü d: Ankara issued a statement backing Georgia's territorial integrity.
en.Türkiye Gürcistan'la (BTC, Kars-Tiflis d: Turkey has ties with both Georgia (BTC, Kars–Tbilisi rail) and Russia (gas, tourism, construction). A good moment to float the 'Caucasus Stability and Cooperation Platform'.
en.7–12 Ağustos 2008: Gürcistan'ın Güney Os: 7–12 August 2008: after Georgia's assault on South Ossetia, Russian forces entered Georgia; in the five-day war Abkhazia and South Ossetia were recognised by Russia. Georgia had been a Moscow target since the early 2000s over Chechen refugees and criticism of the Russian campaign.
en.İki bölgeyi tanı, yaptırımlardan kaç: Recognise the two regions, avoid sanctions
en.Rus birlikleri Gori ve Poti'den çekildi;: Russian forces withdrew from Gori and Poti; permanent bases will be built in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
en.Moskova ateşkesi ihlal edip Gürcistan iç: Moscow violated the ceasefire and advanced deeper; the West reacted fiercely.
en.Askerî olarak kazandınız, diplomatik ola: You won militarily but are diplomatically isolated; recognition of Abkhazia and South Ossetia found support from very few states.
en.Savaşa devam, Batı'dan yardım iste: Fight on and ask for Western help
en.Gürcü yedek birlikleri Tiflis çevresinde: Georgian reserves dug in around Tbilisi.
en.Ordu yenildi, topraklar kaybedildi. Batı: The army has been beaten and territory lost. The West gave verbal support but no military aid. For Saakashvili: rebuild defences or race toward NATO.
en.12 Ağustos'ta Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Sarko: The six-point ceasefire mediated by French President Sarkozy was signed in August; in September Russian troops began pulling out of the interior of Georgia. Sanctions against Moscow stayed limited as the global financial crisis took over the agenda.
en.Rejimi bitir, Ramzan'ı sürdür (tarihî): End the regime and keep Ramzan (historical)
en.Kuzey Kafkasya'ya kalkınma ve güvenlik p: A North Caucasus development and security package
en.Moskova Kuzey Kafkasya için yeni bir fed: Moscow announced a new federal development programme for the North Caucasus.
en.On yıllık savaş resmen bitti; bedeli çok: Ten years of war are officially over; the cost was huge, but Chechnya stayed in Russia. The question now is Ramzan Kadyrov's dependence on Moscow and the violence spreading in other republics.
en.Dağlarda küçük çeteler Rus ve Kadirovtsi: Small bands in the mountains keep attacking Russian and Kadyrovtsy targets.
en.Çeçen komutanların bir kısmı Kadirov'un: Some Chechen commanders took Kadyrov's amnesty.
en.Direniş bölünmüş ve zayıf; bağımsızlık f: The resistance is divided and weak; the independence idea is under Ramzan's pressure. Yet Umarov's Emirate is still standing in the Caucasus.
en.Terörle Mücadele Rejiminin Sonu: The End of the CTO Regime
en.16 Nisan 2009: Medvedev Çeçenistan'daki: 16 April 2009: Medvedev officially ended the 'counter-terrorist operation' regime in Chechnya. Ramzan Kadyrov has full control of the region; Grozny has been rebuilt; yet violence continues in Dagestan, Ingushetia and Kabardino-Balkaria.
